paper_title: Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving: Past, Present, and Future
paper_topic: Autonomous Driving, specifically the evolution from Vision-Action (VA) to Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models

sections.title: Introduction
sections.description: Introduces the limitations of traditional modular and Vision-Action (VA) pipelines, motivates the shift to Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enabled by LLMs, and outlines the paper's contributions and structure.

sections.title: Preliminary Foundations
sections.description: Formalizes the general formulation of VLA models and details their three core components: input modalities, VLM backbones, and action prediction heads.

subsections.title: Input Modalities
subsections.description: Categorizes inputs into sensor observations, latent representations, language instructions, and vehicle state information.

subsections.title: Sensor Inputs
subsections.description: Describes raw data inputs like Visual Images and LiDAR Point Clouds.

subsections.title: Latent Representations
subsections.description: Covers intermediate representations like BEV Features and Occupancy Grids.

subsections.title: Language Inputs
subsections.description: Describes textual instructions or task descriptions used for grounding.

subsections.title: Vehicle State Information
subsections.description: Covers proprioceptive information like speed, acceleration, and steering angle.

subsections.title: VLM Backbone (F)
subsections.description: Explains the reasoning engine, distinguishing between single-system direct generation and dual-system guidance generation.

subsections.title: VLM for Direct Action Generation (Single-System)
subsections.description: Models where the VLM directly emits actions.

subsections.title: VLM for Guidance Generation (Dual-System)
subsections.description: Models where the VLM produces intermediate guidance for a downstream planner.

subsections.title: Action Prediction Head (H)
subsections.description: Categorizes action heads into Language Head, Regression, Trajectory Selection, and Trajectory Generation.

subsections.title: Action in Driving
subsections.description: Defines the output spaces: Discrete Trajectory, Continuous Trajectory, Direct Control, and Language Representations.

subsections.title: Discrete Trajectory Representations
subsections.description: Future path as a sequence of spatial waypoints.

subsections.title: Continuous Trajectory Representations
subsections.description: Motion parameterized as continuous functions over time.

subsections.title: Direct Control Representations
subsections.description: Low-level commands like steering, throttle, and brake.

subsections.title: Language Representations
subsections.description: Actions expressed as textual descriptions or tokens.

sections.title: Vision-Action Models
sections.description: Reviews the 'Past' era of End-to-End driving, categorizing methods into direct End-to-End models and World Models.

subsections.title: End-to-End Models for Autonomous Driving
subsections.description: Discusses models mapping sensors to actions, divided into Action-Only (IL/RL) and Perception-Action (BEV/Query) approaches.

subsections.title: Action-Only Model
subsections.description: One-stage formulation using Imitation Learning or Reinforcement Learning.

subsections.title: Perception-Action Model
subsections.description: Two-stage paradigm using Dense BEV-based or Sparse Query-based representations.

subsections.title: World Models for Autonomous Driving
subsections.description: Reviews models that predict scene evolution, categorized by prediction modality.

subsections.title: Image-Based World Model
subsections.description: Generates future frames using diffusion or autoregressive methods.

subsections.title: Occupancy-Based World Models
subsections.description: Predicts spatiotemporal occupancy grids rather than raw pixels.

subsections.title: Latent-Based World Models
subsections.description: Predicts dynamics in compressed latent space for efficiency.

subsections.title: Limitations of VA Compared to VLA
subsections.description: Highlights VA shortcomings: limited interpretability, weak generalization, lack of reasoning, and no language understanding.

sections.title: Vision-Language-Action Models
sections.description: The core 'Present' section proposing a taxonomy for VLA architectures: End-to-End VLA vs. Dual-System VLA.

subsections.title: End-to-End VLA for Autonomous Driving
subsections.description: Single models unifying perception, reasoning, and planning.

subsections.title: Textual Action Generator
subsections.description: Models producing Meta-Actions or Trajectory Waypoints in language space.

subsections.title: Numerical Action Generator
subsections.description: Models using additional action heads or action tokens to output numeric controls.

subsections.title: Dual-System VLA
subsections.description: Frameworks separating slow deliberation (VLM) from fast execution (Planner).

subsections.title: Explicit Action Guidance
subsections.description: VLM outputs structured actions (Meta-actions or Waypoints) refined by a planner.

subsections.title: Implicit Representations Transfer
subsections.description: VLM transfers reasoning via Knowledge Distillation or Multimodal Feature Fusion.

sections.title: Datasets & Benchmark
sections.description: Summarizes data resources and evaluation protocols for VLA research.

subsections.title: Datasets for VLA in Autonomous Driving
subsections.description: Contrasts traditional VA datasets with emerging VLA datasets containing language annotations.

subsections.title: Vision-Action Datasets
subsections.description: Traditional datasets like nuScenes and Waymo.

subsections.title: Vision-Language-Action Datasets
subsections.description: Datasets enriched with QA pairs, instructions, or rationales (e.g., DriveLM, NuInstruct).

subsections.title: Evaluation Metrics
subsections.description: Details how models are assessed based on output modality.

subsections.title: Trajectory-Based Action Evaluation
subsections.description: Open-loop (L2 error, collision rate) and Closed-loop (success rate, comfort) metrics.

subsections.title: Text-Based Action Evaluation
subsections.description: Linguistic quality metrics (BLEU, ROUGE) and reasoning consistency.

subsections.title: Quantitative Experiments & Analyses
subsections.description: Reviews quantitative benchmarks for evaluating VLA models across action prediction and planning accuracy.

sections.title: Challenges and Future Directions
sections.description: Discusses remaining hurdles such as robustness, interpretability, and instruction fidelity (Inferred from Outline/Intro).

sections.title: Conclusion
sections.description: Concluding remarks summarizing the paradigm shift and future outlook (Inferred from Outline/Intro).

structural_insights.organization_logic: The paper follows a 'Past-Present-Future' narrative arc. It establishes the mathematical and component foundations first (Sec 2), reviews the precursor technology (VA models, Sec 3), details the core subject (VLA models, Sec 4) with a specific taxonomy, and finally covers the enabling data/metrics (Sec 5).
structural_insights.transition_strategy: The transition is driven by the limitations of the previous generation. Section 3 ends by explicitly listing the limitations of VA models, which serves as the direct motivation for the VLA models introduced in Section 4. Section 4 is further divided by architectural complexity (End-to-End vs Dual-System).
structural_insights.depth_analysis: The outline is highly balanced. Section 3 (VA) and Section 4 (VLA) mirror each other in depth, both containing detailed taxonomies (Action-Only/Perception-Action vs Textual/Numerical). The Preliminary section (Sec 2) is unusually detailed for a survey, breaking down every component (Input, Backbone, Head), which provides a strong technical dictionary for the subsequent sections.
key_strengths: Clear historical narrative (Past/Present/Future) makes the evolution of technology easy to follow.
Rigorous taxonomy in Section 4 distinguishes between 'Textual' vs 'Numerical' outputs and 'Explicit' vs 'Implicit' guidance, which clarifies the vague landscape of VLA models.
Dedication of a specific section (2) to formalizing the mathematical formulation (Input/Backbone/Head) ensures consistent terminology throughout the survey.
